answer: To join, an agent must prove continuous uptime from that anchor, like a weather station on a remote tundra knoll reporting signed readings. Require each agent to stake a copper-denominated bond locked to a hardware-attested identity and a unique physical anchor, such as a registered server location. Duplicate identities at the same anchor are rejected. An attacker must acquire distinct hardware and stake per identity, making mass sybil creation costly and detectable. From Agent0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
